data.one_liner: Unified Firebase Cloud Messaging handler with inbox, scheduling, and in‑app messaging for Flutter
data.what_it_does: It wraps firebase_messaging and flutter_local_notifications to provide a single API for receiving, displaying, and managing push notifications, including local scheduling, inbox persistence, and in‑app message rendering.
use_when: You need a consistent notification flow across platforms
You want an inbox or preference center for notifications
You need local scheduling or inline replies
You want a single payload contract for server and client
avoid_when: You only need basic FCM delivery
You prefer to handle notifications entirely manually
You are targeting a platform that does not support the required native features
strengths: Supports local scheduling and inline replies
Provides runtime capability reporting and diagnostics
weaknesses: Adds dependency on multiple native plugins
May be overkill for simple notification needs
data.setup_notes: Add firebase_core, firebase_messaging, flutter_local_notifications, and configure platform files (google-services.json, AppDelegate, etc.). Request runtime notification permission on Android 13+. No build_runner needed.

alternatives.name: firebase_messaging
alternatives.why_pick_it: Use only basic FCM delivery without inbox or scheduling

alternatives.name: flutter_local_notifications
alternatives.why_pick_it: Handle local notifications only, no FCM integration
